messages:
rachel: Heads-up — seeing a noticeable LCP + chart freeze regression on dashboard after the 15:10 rollout. Charts take ~1-2s to start drawing, main thread busy. Repro on prod-canary and eu-prod.

alex: ugh, saw alerts too. stacktrace looks like parse/block on a big CSS chunk? network shows a ~160KB non-critical stylesheet fetched before chart JS.

mike: can you paste the waterfall? Also any change to splitpoints in the deploy?

rachel: here — quick paste from devtools network: 
```
/critical.css  200ms  (60KB)  finish
/non-critical-strings.css  800ms (160KB)  blocking?
/main-chart.chunk.js  queued until styles
```

deply-bot: deploy r2026-15:10 → prod completed by @ci (canary 10%).

song: we changed the client chunking to move a bunch of CSS into a named chunk to reduce initial bundle size, but looks like the loader is still preloading it in some routes. probably a splitpoint heuristic regression.

alex: hmm; could be splitpoint placement + new preload logic causing noncritical CSS to be prioritized. If CSS is fetched before runtime, the parser blocks. Quick idea: revert the preload attribute for that chunk or change webpack splitpoint to lazy.

mike: also seeing a KV cache miss storm on chart data fetches at the same time; routing policy sent more traffic to eu nodes with cold caches during canary bump. That might amplify UI stalls.

rachel: good call. Two levers: 1) stop preloading the non-critical stylesheet 2) throttle canary weight back to 5% and warm kvcache. Which is faster to ship?

song: 1) is a 1-line change in frontend split config: remove <link rel=preload> for chunk X. Can ship as a patch to canary-only rollout. 2) needs infra change + backfill job. I'd do (1) first.

alex: agreed. small PR to remove preload, run canary. If that fixes LCP, we keep and then follow up with cache warmers.

mike: I'm going to kick off a kvcache-warm job for the eu pool. ETA ~10m.

perf-ci: perf regression alert created: dashboard-lcp +0.9s (p50). Traces attached.

rachel: posting repro steps and screenshot in the PR. Also tagging @frontend-team for FYI.

song: PR created: r/patch/remove-css-preload. Will push to canary-only slot in 5m.

deploy-bot: starting deploy r2026-15:40-canary (patch: remove-css-preload)

alex: watching metrics... initial canary looks much better — LCP down ~650ms. charts render faster, main thread idle time reduced.

mike: eu kvcache warm completed. No more miss spikes. Looks stable so far.

rachel: leaving canary at 10% for another 30m then roll forward if stable. Follow-ups: (a) audit splitpoint heuristics to avoid moving noncritical CSS into preloaded slots (b) add a perf test that loads dashboard with cold kvcache + canary churn.

song: logging follow-up infra ticket for splitpoint heuristic and adding an integration perf test.

alex: if we want extra safety, add an automated check in rollout pipeline that flags new preload entries for chunks >50KB.

rachel: agreed — will file. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:

mike: good save. :rocket:
